items.title: Fedwire participant payment or securities-transfer instruction
kv: A Fedwire participant sends a Funds payment order or Securities transfer message under the applicable service’s legal framework.
Fedwire Funds: Regulation J and OC 6. Fedwire Securities: applicable book-entry securities regulations and OC 7.

Identify the eligible participant, its Reserve Bank account or securities account, and the exact Fedwire service. · Apply the service's authorization/security procedure, message format, account, asset, and cutoff conditions. · For securities, establish Fedwire eligibility and any transfer-against-payment conditions; for funds, establish a payment order accepted under the applicable procedure.

Fedwire Funds participant or authorized sender under its service arrangement · Fedwire Securities participant · authorized service provider acting through the participant's applicable Fedwire arrangement
This is a Fedwire-specific authorization route. A wallet signature, API call, or message on another system does not inherit Fedwire authority or establish legal effect for a different claim.

items.title: FedLine electronic-access and designated service-provider route
kv: A Reserve Bank institution or authorized service provider accesses an identified Reserve Bank electronic service through the applicable OC 5 and service terms.
Operating Circular 5 and the relevant Fedwire service terms; the Fedwire form route expressly contemplates designation of a third-party service provider.

Identify the institution, electronic connection, access credentials, and exact Reserve Bank service. · Recover the applicable OC 5/service terms and any third-party service arrangement or API terms. · Establish separately the participant that has authority to originate the payment or securities instruction and the service-specific acceptance/finality event.
Reserve Bank service participant · FedLine subscriber · Reserve Bank-authorized API service provider · designated Fedwire third-party service provider

This is an authorized Reserve Bank electronic-access route, not a general interoperability license. Electronic transport does not make the provider the account holder, sender, securities participant, title authority, or settlement obligor.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Operating Circular 5 electronic access and API terms

items.title: Registered transfer agent using DLT in its official record
kv: A registered transfer agent uses DLT for all or part of its official master securityholder file for a covered security.
SEC staff DLT FAQ Q10–Q11, Exchange Act transfer-agent framework, and the transfer agent's existing applicable recordkeeping and safeguarding duties.

Identify the registered transfer agent, covered security, issuer appointment, and official master securityholder file. · Establish how the on-chain and off-chain components together remain secure, accurate, current, producible, and retained as required. · Recover the applicable correction, reconciliation, fork, access, and vendor-control procedures.
SEC-registered transfer agent · bank transfer agent registered with the appropriate federal banking regulator

The FAQ does not provide a standalone legal-effect route for a generic network operator, validator, sequencer, bridge, or protocol-governance group. Their legal effect remains a separate arrangement-specific question.

items.title: Technology vendor or outsourced infrastructure under accountable-client controls
kv: Circle Technology Services, LLC · Arc Network Services LLC
A regulated or contractually accountable firm uses a vendor, linked ledger, database, wallet system, or infrastructure provider to perform part of its operating model.

Service contract plus the accountable client's applicable statutory and regulatory obligations. For supervised banking organizations, SR 23-4 gives risk-management guidance for third-party relationships and explicitly creates no new requirements.

Identify the client that retains the regulated or contractual duty. · Recover the vendor agreement, data/control access, security, continuity, audit, incident, correction, and exit provisions. · Test the vendor's own activity separately if it also performs a regulated function.
software vendor · cloud or infrastructure provider · ledger/database provider · wallet or key-management vendor · systems integrator · recordkeeping transfer agent using linked technical systems

Vendor participation does not relocate a regulated client's recordkeeping, reporting, safeguarding, or examination duties, and it does not prove the vendor holds an independent regulatory permission. SR 23-4 is guidance, not a new vendor authorization rule.

sources.label: Federal Reserve SR 23-4 interagency third-party relationship guidance
SEC staff FAQ on registered transfer agents' use of distributed ledger technology
